title: Platform Vote #9 (demo)
description: A demo built from the USTP's Platform Vote #9 ballot (February 17 to March 10, 2025): all 20 questions, with the same 21-day window. The summaries are ours, not the official text, which is at https://transhumanist-party.org/2025/02/18/ballot-options-platform-vote-9/. Where that ballot sets no threshold, this demo uses a majority of yes and no votes.

contests.title: Question I. Section E9-A: Defeat of COVID as a priority

proposal.body:
Adds a platform section making the defeat of COVID-19 as a public-health threat a priority, pursued through science and technology.

A summary for this demo, not the official text, which is at https://transhumanist-party.org/2025/02/18/ballot-options-platform-vote-9/

contests.title: Question II. Provisions to add to Section E9-A (select all you support)
contests.description:
Each provision a majority of ballots supports is added, unless No wins Question I.

E9-A-i: a vaccine that works against every variant and gives lasting immunity.
E9-A-ii: engineered harmless variants that outcompete the harmful ones.
E9-A-iii: antibodies that neutralize any variant.
E9-A-iv: reliable cures for every form of Long COVID.

contests.title: Question III. Provision E9-A-Add-1: Science, not restrictions

proposal.body:
Adds to Section E9-A that COVID-19 should be fought with science and technology alone: no lockdowns or limits on liberty or medical choice, no stigma for people who take precautions, and nobody pushed into riskier behavior.

A summary for this demo, not the official text, which is at https://transhumanist-party.org/2025/02/18/ballot-options-platform-vote-9/

contests.title: Question IV. Section E9-B: Artificial intelligence (rank the options)
contests.description:
E9-B-1: treat AI chiefly as an opportunity, support safety research and a ban on autonomous weapons, and oppose coercing individuals or countries to halt AI development.
E9-B-2: the same, but the clause against coercion covers individuals only.
E9-B-3: generally in favor of AI, with debate on uses that threaten livelihoods or safety.
E9-B-NO: add no section of this sort.

Rank as many as you like; ranking none abstains.
candidates: E9-B-1: Opportunity; no coercion of people or countries
E9-B-2: Opportunity; no coercion of people
E9-B-3: Pro-AI, with debate on risky uses
E9-B-NO: No section of this sort

contests.title: Question V. Provisions to add to Section E9-B (select all you support)
contests.description:
Each provision a majority of ballots supports is added.

E9-B-i: AI policy must address unintended bias, so that AI systems do not discriminate by race, sex or similar traits.
E9-B-ii: no AI in law enforcement, such as facial recognition that misidentifies people.
candidates: E9-B-ii: No AI in law enforcement

contests.title: Question VI. Section E9-C: Reversible cryopreservation

proposal.body:
Calls for $10 billion a year of research funding for reversible cryopreservation.

A summary for this demo, not the official text, which is at https://transhumanist-party.org/2025/02/18/ballot-options-platform-vote-9/

contests.title: Question VII. Section E9-D: Public money for public code

proposal.body:
Public money should go to open-source software and the people who contribute to it, with safeguards so that companies cannot crowd out individual developers.

A summary for this demo, not the official text, which is at https://transhumanist-party.org/2025/02/18/ballot-options-platform-vote-9/

contests.title: Question VIII. Section E9-E: Privacy on social media

proposal.body:
Supports clearer, finer-grained and more visible privacy controls for the people who use social media.

A summary for this demo, not the official text, which is at https://transhumanist-party.org/2025/02/18/ballot-options-platform-vote-9/

contests.title: Question IX. Section E9-F: Government and business security (rank the options)
contests.description:
E9-F-1: government agencies should not undermine the security measures companies take.
E9-F-2: the same, and agencies may not ask companies to build hidden access into their software.
E9-F-3: the same as E9-F-1, without standing in the way of needed federal regulation of business, large corporations especially.
E9-F-NO: add no section of this sort.

Rank as many as you like; ranking none abstains.
candidates: E9-F-2: Restrain government; no backdoor requests
E9-F-3: Restrain government; regulation still allowed
E9-F-NO: No section of this sort

contests.title: Question X. Section E9-G: Security whistleblower program

proposal.body:
Supports a program for reporting security problems that go unaddressed, with protection against retaliation by employers.

A summary for this demo, not the official text, which is at https://transhumanist-party.org/2025/02/18/ballot-options-platform-vote-9/

contests.title: Question XI. Section XXVII: Electing the President
contests.description:
Current: abolish the Electoral College, so that a plurality of the national popular vote decides the presidency.
XXVII-1: still abolish the Electoral College, but decide by ranked-preference voting or a similar method instead of plurality.

Leave it blank to abstain.

contests.title: Question XII. Section XXXVI: No sales tax on life necessities

proposal.body:
Section XXXVI would replace income taxes with a sales tax on large businesses' purchases. This adds that life necessities, goods used up soon and needed chiefly to survive, are exempt from it.

A summary for this demo, not the official text, which is at https://transhumanist-party.org/2025/02/18/ballot-options-platform-vote-9/

contests.title: Question XIII. Section LXXIX: Right to try
contests.description:
Current: repeal the FDA-approval requirement for treatments that willing patients want to use.
LXXIX-1: call for wider access to unapproved treatments, protection from liability, and a right to try that reaches beyond terminally ill patients.

Leave it blank to abstain.
candidates: Amendment LXXIX-1: Wider right to try

contests.title: Question XIV. Section XCIX: COVID relief
contests.description:
Current: a universal basic income of at least $1,000 a month during COVID-19 and its aftermath.
XCIX-1: replace it with free COVID-19 testing, vaccination, antivirals and related care, with no end date.

Leave it blank to abstain.
candidates: Amendment XCIX-1: Free COVID care instead

contests.title: Question XV. Section CI: Air travel
contests.description:
Current: let most waiting travelers through airport checkpoints quickly, with any later health screening done without crowding.
CI-1: also tackle airline delays by restoring capacity, rehiring staff and keeping staffing and flights at pre-COVID levels.

Leave it blank to abstain.

contests.title: Question XVI. Section CII: Troops overseas (rank the options)
contests.description:
Current: bring overseas U.S. military personnel home to build hospitals, deliver emergency aid and work on infrastructure.
CII-1: recall troops from abroad except those needed to defend American assets and citizens or to meet limited treaty obligations, and give troops at home crisis-response roles.
CII-2: the same, but keep abroad only troops defending American citizens or meeting treaty duties.

Rank as many as you like; ranking none abstains.
candidates: CII-1: Recall, keeping defense of assets and citizens
CII-2: Recall, keeping defense of citizens only

contests.title: Question XVII. Section CIII: COVID cures and vaccines
contests.description:
Current: fast research into COVID-19 cures and vaccines, funded and owned by the government and given out free, with a $100 billion vaccine package.
CIII-1: put the emphasis on lasting cures and on vaccines that work against every variant, released into the public domain.

Leave it blank to abstain.
candidates: Amendment CIII-1: Lasting, all-variant, public domain

contests.title: Question XVIII. Section CIV: Anti-aging research (rank the options)
contests.description:
Current: aging is the leading risk factor for death and for severe COVID-19; fund anti-aging research with $100 billion a year, permanently.
CIV-1 and CIV-2: keep the funding, add the disabilities that aging brings, and treat aging as a violation of the rights to life and health. They differ only in one conjunction.

Rank as many as you like; ranking none abstains.

contests.title: Question XIX. Section CX: COVID testing
contests.description:
Current: widespread free COVID-19 testing, help for the makers of tests, and at-home kits mailed to labs.
CX-1: continuous testing with no end date, credit for the home-test approach, and a return to the data collection of the early pandemic.

Leave it blank to abstain.
candidates: Amendment CX-1: Continuous testing and data

contests.title: Question XX. Investigations and emergency declarations (rank the options)
contests.description:
These would form a new Article of the Constitution.

ZR-JG-1: in an emergency the Chairman may act and speak for the party, with limits on compelling retractions and good-faith efforts to let the Chairman answer attacks.
RNS-1 and RNS-2, one package: neutrality during outside investigations and only impartial internal investigators; emergencies defined narrowly, and membership approval for emergency actions longer than 14 days.
Adopt neither: keep things as they are.

Rank as many as you like; ranking none abstains.
candidates: ZR-JG-1: Decisive executive action in emergencies
RNS-1 and RNS-2: Neutral investigations, limited emergencies
